findings: Many faces are ambiguous rather than mapping to one emotion only.
Dominant emotion used rating frequency, with mean intensity as tie-break.
Expression variety increased dramatically beginning around the 1989 Pirates era.
Context significantly influenced perceived anger, disgust, sadness and surprise.
Skin-color variation did not significantly change perceived emotional expression.
Cluster analysis identified disdain, confidence, concern, fear, happiness and anger.

findings: Individual differences in observers were more important than emotional category for parts of perception.
44 of 92 analyzed figures received all six emotion labels at least once; another 31 received five of six.
Perceived expression labels are therefore probabilistic/distributed rather than objectively singular.
